steps.what: List stored fields for bank cards and checks
Carry out special services for customers
Complete the ordering of bank cards and checks
Sign the card or check order
Send only the signed card order
outputs: filed copy of signed card order v1

tasks.design: A job lists the stored fields in {BANK}. The teller carries out the special service and completes the ordering of bank cards and checks. A later job sends only the signed order. It does not order a card by itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Card orders were retyped into a message.
tasks.enabler_now: Customer identifier and card type are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The customer is still served at the window.
tasks.altitude: The teller spends the week with the customer, not on listing the fields.

reach.task: Receive only the order the teller signed

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a person keeps persuading and the payment release.

assumptions: Customer identifier, card type, and check quantity are stored on the order record. The order record produces them. A blank card type stays blank and is not ordered.
Native configuration of the order record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the teller signed is filed or sent.
The send is the signed order and no other card.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining service is still the teller carrying out the special service.

incremental.description: Refresh customer identifier and card type when the order layout changes, and drop an order the teller has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many card types are blank. The high end assumes customer identifier and card type are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Sort and file slips by hand.

steps.what: Order stored deposit slips and checks by account
Sort deposit slips and checks by hand
File the paper slips and checks
Sign the filing note
File the signed filing note
outputs: filed copy of signed filing note v1

tasks.design: A job orders stored deposit slips and checks in {DOCS} by account. The teller still sorts and files the paper. A later job files the signed note. The paper work is unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: The order was written on a cover sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Slip identifier and account are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The paper is still sorted by hand.
tasks.human_edge: The teller decides the file is complete.
tasks.altitude: The teller spends the week on the paper, not on ordering the list.

reach.task: Keep only the note the teller signed

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a person keeps persuading and the payment release.

assumptions: Slip identifier, account, and document type are stored on the filing record. The filing record produces them. A blank account stays blank and is shown as a gap.
Native configuration of the filing record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the teller signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining sort is still the teller sorting slips and checks.

incremental.description: Refresh slip identifier and account when the filing layout changes, and drop a note the teller has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many account identifiers are blank. The high end assumes slip identifier and account are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Compare daily inventories with the stored count
Receive and count cash, drafts, and travelers' checks
Judge whether the daily inventories are complete
Sign the inventory count
File the signed inventory count
outputs: filed copy of signed inventory count v1

tasks.design: A job compares the daily inventories in {BANK} with the stored count. The teller receives and counts the cash, drafts, and travelers' checks. A later job files the signed count in {DOCS}. It does not treat a blank count as zero.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inventory lines were copied before the count.
tasks.enabler_now: Item identifier and stored count are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The items are still counted by hand.
tasks.human_edge: The teller decides the inventory is complete.
tasks.altitude: The teller spends the week on the count, not on the comparison.

reach.task: Accept only the inventory the teller signed

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a person keeps persuading and the payment release.
The executive digest says a match is posted only on an exact amount, and any miss stops with a person.

assumptions: Item identifier, item kind, and stored count are stored on the inventory record. The inventory record produces them. A blank count stays blank and is not treated as zero.
Native configuration of the inventory record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the teller signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining count is still the teller counting cash, drafts, and travelers' checks.

incremental.description: Refresh item identifier and stored count when the inventory layout changes, and drop a count the teller has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many stored counts are blank. The high end assumes item identifier and stored count are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order cash only after a signature.

steps.what: List the stored cash total against daily needs
Decide the cash supply for daily needs
Order that supply only after the count
Sign the cash supply order
Send only the signed cash order
outputs: filed copy of signed cash order v1

tasks.design: A job lists the stored cash total in {BANK} against daily needs. The teller decides the supply and orders it. A later job sends only the signed order. It does not order cash by itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The order amount was retyped into a message.
tasks.enabler_now: Vault identifier and stored total are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The teller still chooses the supply.
tasks.human_edge: The teller decides how much cash to order.
tasks.altitude: The teller spends the week on the order, not on listing the total.

reach.task: Send only the supply the teller signed

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a person keeps persuading and the payment release.

assumptions: Vault identifier, stored total, and daily need are stored on the vault record. The vault record produces them. A blank total stays blank and is not ordered as zero.
Native configuration of the vault record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the teller signed is filed or sent.
The send is the signed supply and no other amount.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining decision is still the teller deciding the cash supply.

incremental.description: Refresh vault identifier and stored total when the vault layout changes, and drop an order the teller has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many stored totals are blank. The high end assumes vault identifier and stored total are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teller spends the week at the window, on the cash, and on the signed amount. A stored total, a fee from a stored rule, and filing that signature can move. The teller still counts the cash, checks the signature, and releases the payment.
reach: A customer receives only the amount the teller signed.
A colleague posts only the deposit the teller signed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a payout that the teller has not signed.
Reject a fee that does not match the stored rule.
Reject a balance that treats a blank amount as zero.
role.ambitious_version: A signed payout or statement can go out the same day, and the teller still owns the cash.
